card.name: hammerdb-rhel9-rootdisk-grp
card.role: the request for the root disk

def.what: A request for storage, written by whoever runs the application.
def.creator: The application owner, or a DataVolume preparing a disk for a guest.
def.reader: Kubernetes and the storage plugin. Ramen lists these to decide what to protect.
def.where: The workload namespace, hammerdb, on each cluster.
def.analogy: An order slip for a disk. It is not the disk and it is not the ledger entry.

card.name: csivol-31136f5c90
card.role: the ledger entry that names the real disk and its delete policy

def.what: The cluster-wide record of one real disk. It holds the disk handle and the delete policy.
def.creator: The storage plugin, when a claim is bound.
def.reader: Kubernetes volume controller, the storage plugin, and Ramen when it protects the claim.
def.where: Cluster scope on the cluster that owns the disk.
def.analogy: The ledger entry that carries the serial number of the thing in the storeroom, plus a note saying whether it may be scrapped.

card.name: hammerdb-drpc
card.role: tells one cluster what its job is for this application

def.what: The per-cluster work order for one application. Its state field says Primary or Secondary.
def.creator: The hub placement controller, which writes the state into the cluster manifest.
def.reader: The Ramen controller on that cluster, and the hub when it checks readiness.
def.analogy: A shift assignment posted at one factory. Head office writes it. The factory only reads it.

card.name: vgr-4251c970ec7af885d6ec79c1d2c40661-hammerdb-drpc
card.role: the request that drives one array session for the whole group

def.what: One request covering every disk of a group, so the array moves them together.
def.creator: The Ramen controller on the cluster that holds the claims.
def.reader: The storage replication sidecar, which turns it into an array call.
def.where: The workload namespace, hammerdb, on the cluster that owns the claims.
def.analogy: One shipping order for a pallet. It is not the pallet and it is not the truck.
